messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: detectCores under Windows
parts:
RSTan Version 2.7.0.1 Windows 64 bit on I7 Processor with 4 logical and a total of 8 cores:


Under the above configuration, using parallel::detectCores() is not recommended, it gives 8 and a performance worse than 4 
because of overhead. Note that this is not an effect of setup, with 32 seconds setup is negligible. 

> options(mc.cores = 4)
> system.time(fit6 <- stan("horseshoe6.stan", data = d, iter = 30000, thin = 10,
+             pars = c("beta","lambda")))
   user  system elapsed 
   0.17    0.24   28.28 
> options(mc.cores = 8)
> system.time(fit6 <- stan("horseshoe6.stan", data = d, iter = 30000, thin = 10,
+             pars = c("beta","lambda")))
   user  system elapsed 
   0.30    0.59   32.92

The problem is in documentation: while it says that logical = FALSE is the default, in fact it is not:

> parallel::detectCores()
[1] 8
> parallel::detectCores(logical=FALSE)
[1] 4

Recommended setting under my configuration is:

options(mc.cores= parallel::detectCores(logical=FALSE))

Dieter

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: detectCores under Windows
parts:
On Monday, August 3, 2015 at 5:01:21 AM UTC-4, Dieter Menne wrote:
RSTan Version 2.7.0.1 Windows 64 bit on I7 Processor with 4 logical and a total of 8 cores:


Under the above configuration, using parallel::detectCores() is not recommended, it gives 8 and a performance worse than 4 
because of overhead. Note that this is not an effect of setup, with 32 seconds setup is negligible.

That is possible, but test it passing the arguments chains = 8 and seed = something both times you call stan(). By default, stan() only does 4 chains, so using 8 logical cores in that case is not going to help more than just using 4 physical cores. But also, wall times are highly variable for Stan programs, so you need to call it with the same seed to ensure that it is taking the same number of leapfrog steps over the course of the run.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] detectCores under Windows
parts:
What Ben said about evaluation. Plus...

I think it's worth detecting the physical cores if possible. In every
experiment I've ever done, concurrency exceeding the physical
cores slows things down in scientific computing (when each thread
or process is banging away hammer and tongs). My guess is that
it's too much memory contention and/or too much context switching
into the physical cores.

For reasons Ben mentioned, the killer isn't a 4-core machine running
the default 4 chains. But I think it is a big problem for 2-core
machines (like the ubiquitous core duos on compact notebooks), where
running 4 chains will try to use the hyperthreading. Assuming that is
that the 2-core core duos report 4 cores available.

- Bob
